An extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding

Extriangulated categories, introduced by Nakaoka and Palu, axiomatize the extension-closed subcategories of triangulated categories. Gorsky, Nakaoka and Palu asked whether every extriangulated category arises this way. It does not: over every field there is a small, well-behaved extriangulated category that admits no fully faithful extriangulated functor into any triangulated category. All of this is checked in Lean.

Theorem A. Over every field k there is an essentially small k-linear extriangulated category 𝒞 such that (1) 𝒞 has no triangulated embedding; (2) every countable family of objects of 𝒞 lies in a full extension-closed subcategory with an algebraic realization; (3) 𝒞 is hereditary and Krull–Schmidt, has enough injectives and ℵ1 isomorphism classes of indecomposables, each with endomorphism ring k, dim 𝔼(C, A) ≤ 1 for indecomposables A, C, and every morphism space has at most countable dimension.
Theorem B. For an inverse system D of vector spaces with surjective transition maps over an ordinal I, the category 𝒞(D) has a triangulated embedding if and only if every projection lim D → Di is surjective, if and only if 𝒞(D) has an algebraic realization.

Verification and provenance

The category 𝒞(D)

Adjoin a least point * to the ordinal I and take the interval representations Y = k{*}, Ai = k[0,i] and Pi = k[*,i], with the sequences 0 → Ai → Pi → Y → 0. Adjoin one more object X with Hom(X, Ai) = Di, composition with Aj → Ai given by the transition maps, and all other morphisms from or to X zero except the scalars. The extension bifunctor is Ext1 of the representations, with X sent to zero. A triangulated embedding sends the sequences Ai → Pi → Y to triangles with the common third term Y; every element of Di factors through a morphism from the shift of X to Y, and composing that morphism with all the connecting morphisms gives a compatible family. So the projections from lim D must be surjective.

The example

For Theorem A, Di = k(Ti) over the countable ordinals, where Ti is the i-th level of an Aronszajn tree of bounded increasing rational sequences (Jech). The levels are countable, so the morphism spaces are countable-dimensional; there is no branch, so lim D = 0 by a finite-support argument (Bergman, Higman–Stone), while D0 = k.

What is formalized

Every numbered statement of the paper is formalized, together with the cited inputs the proofs use: the axioms of extriangulated categories, the algebraicity of homotopy categories, Bergman's lemma and Jech's tree. The correspondence record maps each numbered statement to its Lean declarations.

A Mathlib-only file defines extriangulated categories and functors, triangulated embeddings and algebraic realizations, and the category 𝒞(D).
